diagnosis.summary: order-api 5xx ratio rose to 95% after a new rollout revision 28 with a new faults ConfigMap (same image). Analysis aborted the rollout, and logs show missing relation 'orders' in Postgres. Config link unverified.

probable_cause.statement: The new order-api configuration version (revision 28 with ConfigMap order-api-faults-96ffc8d22c) is the most likely trigger. Errors are caused by the database lacking the 'orders' table, which the config may have changed behaviour around. The ConfigMap contents were not read, so this link is unconf…

supporting.statement: A new rollout revision and ConfigMap were created about 12 minutes before the incident, with the image unchanged, so the change was configuration-only.
The error-rate analysis failed and the rollout was aborted at 11:50:08, showing the new revision was unhealthy.
order-api logs and Postgres both report the 'orders' relation does not exist, matching the 500 errors seen by loadgen.
order-api p95 latency and 5xx ratio moved sharply against the one-hour baseline, while risk-engine stayed error-free.
Request volume to order-api rose roughly fifteen-fold, which may amplify the failure but does not explain the missing table.
Startup probe failures during rollout are common and do not by themselves indicate the fault.

missing_evidence: ConfigMap order-api-faults-96ffc8d22c contents were not read, so the specific fault or config change is unknown.
No database migration or schema history was provided to explain why the 'orders' table is missing.
Unclear whether the aborted revision 28 is still serving traffic or whether the errors continue after rollback.
No timeline linking the rollout abort at 11:50 to the first 5xx errors; metrics show only a before and now snapshot.
Postgres state and recent changes to the database were not provided.

reasons: confidence medium: a human approves first
revert gitops commit 4084022 (Argo CD app sentinel-staging), cited as E1
